test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 05 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution refers to the Rights of Ministers with respect to the State Legislature?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 177.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 177- Rights of Ministers and Advocate-General with respect to the state legislature.**

 
 
• Every Minister and the Advocate-General for a State shall have the right to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, the Legislative Assembly of the State or, in the case of a State having a Legislative Council, both Houses, and to speak in, and otherwise to take part in the proceedings of, any committee of the Legislature of which he may be named a member, but shall not, by virtue of this article, be entitled to vote.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **state legislature consists of the governor and one or two houses.**

 
 
• Where it has two houses:
 
 
• The first house is the **Legislative Assembly.**
 
• The second house is the **Legislative Council**.
 
 
 
 
 
• At present, there are **bicameral legislatures in Bihar, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana**.
 
• Article **168 of the Indian Constitution provides for a legislature in the state.**
 
• According to **Article 169, a Legislative Council **can be constituted in a State
 
• According to Article 171 of the Constitution, the total number of members of the Legislative Council shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State, but this strength should not be less than 40.
